subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept this one-way macOS PortGuardian storage cutover, including signed mixed-version exclusion and no supported rollback to a JSON-only app copy sharing the same state directory?
rationale: The implementation deliberately changes durable state interoperability and uses a code-signing-derived fail-closed boundary; test success cannot decide whether that upgrade and rollback contract is acceptable for supported macOS users.

options.title: Accept the bounded cutover after proof
options.body: Approve the SQLite-only runtime and signed mixed-copy exclusion once the prerequisite lands and inspectable final-head macOS proof confirms the stated recovery paths.

options.title: Preserve an explicit compatibility path
options.body: Require a maintainer-defined upgrade or rollback path if supported mixed-version or downgrade operation must continue.

options.title: Defer the migration
options.body: Pause this branch until the desired durable-state and mixed-version ownership policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded cutover after proof
recommendation.body: Approve the SQLite-only runtime and signed mixed-copy exclusion once the prerequisite lands and inspectable final-head macOS proof confirms the stated recovery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor is actively carrying both this branch and the directly coupled native-state prerequisite, and can clarify the implementation contract for owner review.
